# Policy history + rollback

<!-- Generated by `go run docs/roadmap/gen.go docs` from tickets.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

**Phase:** [P1 · Who did it](../README.md#phase-1--who-did-it) · **Lane:** Control plane · **Label:** `feature:policy-versioning` · **Epic:** [#41](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/41) · **Tickets:** 12 (8S 4M)

Policy and distributed settings move from in-place edits of the served YAML into an append-only versioned store in CP state. Every save creates a new version with author and message, admins can diff any two versions and roll back, and workers are always served the head version. The feature is behind `--policy-store=versioned` (default `file`), credential values are never stored in versions, and the served YAML is kept as a mirror of head so turning the flag off or downgrading the binary serves the same policy. The default flips to versioned in release N+1, and YAML as a policy source is removed in release N+2.

## How we build it

- Gate: new `warden control-plane --policy-store=file|versioned` flag, default `file`. `versioned` requires `--state-dir` (the writable copy of the served config) and the cpstate DB from W-P1-SSO-01, and fails at startup with an actionable error without them. In `file` mode, or with no state dir, the CP keeps today's YAML serve, edit and 3s re-read path byte-for-byte (without `--state-dir` the dashboard keeps rewriting `--config` in place). Release plan: release N (the first release with this feature) ships versioned only behind `--policy-store=versioned`, default `file`. Release N+1 flips the default to `versioned`; `--policy-store=file` stays as an explicit opt-out, and a CP started without `--state-dir` keeps file mode with a startup WARN. Release N+2 removes YAML as a policy source: `--policy-store=file` is removed, the served YAML is only the write-through mirror of head, and hand edits are never served (they come in through `warden policy import`).
- Schema (cpstate migrations): `policy_versions(version INTEGER PK, parent_version, created_at, author_sub, author_email, author_kind (the W-P1-AAUD-01 auth_method set: oidc|breakglass|cli|bearer|none|system), message <=512 chars, source[policy|settings|llmproviders|rollback|import], doc_json, doc_sha256)`, a one-row `policy_head(version)`, and an append-only `policy_publish_log(seq INTEGER PK, version, etag, reason, actor_sub, at)` written in the same transaction as every head move. No code path updates or deletes version rows. Later features use publish_log: signed bundles take seq as their monotonic number, explain resolves a timestamp to a version, and the CP appends a row whenever the served ETag changes without a new version (block-list edits from W-P1-BLOCK-03, AWS credential rotation), so ETag-to-version lookups never miss.
- doc_json is the canonical policyWire {allowlist, denylist, settings}. Credential values are never versioned: a non-empty `settings.secrets.secretAccessKey` (internal/config/settings.go, the sanctioned credential-on-wire exception) is replaced by `sha256:<16 hex>` before hashing and storing. The live value stays in the CP-local served YAML secretStore block, as today, and is overlaid when the served wire is built through the serve-time overlay seam (W-P1-PVER-11), so /policy bytes and the worker behaviour are unchanged. `blockedUsers` (W-P1-BLOCK-01/03) is also excluded from doc_json and merged in at serve time by its own overlay, so rollback can never unblock a user. The /policy ETag is the hash of the merged served wire, not doc_sha256.
- `PolicyVersionStore` is an interface (Create, Head, Get, List, PublishLog, AppendPublish) with a SQLite implementation so a later Postgres store can implement it. Create is one transaction: insert the version, `UPDATE policy_head SET version=new WHERE version=expectedHead` (0 rows means ErrConflict and rollback of the transaction), append the publish_log row. This compare-and-swap works across processes, so the CLI and the CP cannot both create the same version. A doc whose doc_sha256 equals head's writes nothing and returns changed=false. Ordering always uses the version integer, never created_at.
- Validation reuses the existing full loader, not a parallel validator: render the candidate (served YAML root with its policy and settings blocks replaced by the doc, using the encoders WritePolicy/WriteSettings use today), write a temp file and run config.NewLocalYAMLProvider, the same check atomicWriteConfig makes. This enforces default-deny (empty allowlist rejected), domain and rate-limit checks and cross-block references such as judge/explore llmProvider. Save, import and rollback all go through it, and a failure returns 422 with the loader error and leaves head unchanged.
- One publish path: `s.publish(ctx, mutate func(*policyWire), expectedHead, msg, source)` runs under writeMu. WritePolicy (allow/deny), WriteSettings (the blocks its form owns) and WriteLLMProviders (llmProviders) each change only their own fields and carry every other wire field from head (dlp, advisory, explore and so on). CP-local writers (WriteIntegrations, WriteDetection, console) keep the YAML round-trip. A test asserts every SettingsWire field is either owned by a writer or carried.
- Serving: policyServer.loadPolicy returns head doc plus credential overlay plus blockedUsers, held in the in-memory policyWatch. The /policy hot path never touches the DB. Create calls Refresh so long-poll waiters wake at once. In versioned mode the existing 3s ticker runs `SELECT version FROM policy_head` and reloads the doc only when the version changes, so out-of-process writes (CLI) reach workers within 3s plus one long-poll cycle.
- Degraded modes: startup in versioned mode is fail-closed. If the store cannot be read, head points at a missing version, or a doc fails its doc_sha256 check, the CP refuses to start with an actionable error and never falls back to the possibly older YAML. A runtime read error keeps last-known-good in memory (as policyWatch does today) and logs. Workers are unaffected: they keep last-known-good.
- Write-through mirror: after every head move, the CP renders head's policy and settings blocks into the served YAML through atomicWriteConfig and records the mirrored file hash. The YAML therefore always equals head, which makes `--policy-store=file` or a binary downgrade serve the same policy. A mirror failure (for example a read-only mount) logs at error and never fails the version. If the ticker finds the YAML blocks differ from the mirrored hash, that is an external edit: log a warning once per distinct file hash, show a dashboard banner, keep serving head. External edits come back in through `warden policy import`. In file mode (the default) hand edits are still served as today and are audited by W-P1-AAUD-08 as `config.external_change`.
- Migration (W-P1-PVER-07): in versioned mode with an empty store, the CP imports the served YAML's allow/deny and config.SettingsWireFromPolicy (credential redacted) as version 1, author `system:import`, and checks that the served /policy bytes and ETag are unchanged. It is idempotent: a non-empty store is never re-imported.
- Concurrency contract: GET /dashboard/api/policy and /dashboard/api/settings return `version` in the body and an `X-Warden-Policy-Version: N` header. Writes send `If-Match: "v<N>"`. A stale value returns 409 `{error:"policy_conflict", head, author}` (409, not 412, so the body can name the conflicting author). Policy, settings and llmProviders share one head, so a settings save makes a concurrent allow/deny save conflict. Missing If-Match is accepted until W-P1-PVER-04 makes the UI always send it, then returns 428 in versioned mode. The contract is W-P1-PVER-08. /policy's content-hash ETag is unchanged.
- Authors: OIDC sessions record sub and email from the request Principal (W-P1-SSO-04). console.auth none records `anonymous` with author_kind none (dashboard writes there carry the CP admin bearer, which proves possession of a shared token, not an identity); a break-glass session records `breakglass:<username>` with author_kind breakglass. Migration records `system:import`. The CLI records `cli:<os user>`. Messages are capped at 512 characters with control characters stripped.
- Rollback to N creates version latest+1 with N's doc, source `rollback`, message `rollback to v<N>` plus an optional user note. It requires If-Match, is revalidated against today's rules (422 if N no longer validates), and keeps the current credential and block list. History is never rewritten.
- Diff is structural. Allow and deny lists are multisets keyed by a new exported `DiffKey()` method (W-P1-PVER-09) on config.AllowlistEntry and config.DenylistEntry, which today returns domain|port (rateLimit and timeWindow are compared attributes, duplicates show as count changes). W-P1-GPOL-01 extends DiffKey when it adds groups/users. Settings are compared by JSON path into {added, removed, changed}, and credential paths only ever show fingerprints.
- Audit and observability: each save, rollback, import and migration writes an admin audit row with target `policy` and before/after `v<N>:<doc_sha256>`, through a `policy` StateHasher for HTTP paths (W-P1-PVER-08 with W-P1-AAUD-02) and direct appends for migration (W-P1-PVER-07) and the CLI (W-P1-PVER-06, via `adminaudit.OpenForCLI`). slog `policy version created` carries version, parent, source, author_sub and doc_sha256, never doc content or settings values. The fleet view shows each worker's version by mapping its heartbeat ETag through policy_publish_log (W-P1-PVER-10). Metrics hooks (head version, store errors) are noted for when CP metrics exist. P1 has no pruning; growth is one row per save.

## Done when

On a CP started with `--state-dir` and `--policy-store=versioned`, an existing deployment upgrades and serves byte-identical /policy JSON as version 1. Editors make three saves (policy, settings and llmProviders), each shown as a version with author, message and a structural diff, and a concurrent stale save gets 409. Rolling back to version 1 creates version 5, workers pull it within one long-poll cycle, and the fleet view shows them on v5. The served YAML mirrors head, so restarting with `--policy-store=file` serves the same policy. The block list is unchanged by the rollback, every step has an admin audit row, and no policy_versions row or history API response contains a raw AWS secretAccessKey. docs/control-plane.md states the release plan: versioned behind `--policy-store` in release N, the versioned default in N+1, and YAML-as-source removed in N+2.

### 1/12 · W-P1-PVER-01

**Add versioned policy store and serve the head version**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#42](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/42)

**Context.** Policy history moves allow/deny policy and distributed settings from in-place edits of the served YAML into an append-only versioned store in the CP state DB, behind `--policy-store=file|versioned` (default `file`). This ticket is the foundation: the cpstate migrations, the `PolicyVersionStore` with its compare-and-swap `Create`, credential redaction, validation through the existing loader, the flag, and serving the head version. It writes no versions on its own, so with an empty store or in `file` mode behaviour is unchanged. Siblings in the Policy history + rollback feature (epic #41): W-P1-PVER-11 serve-time overlay seam, W-P1-PVER-01 (#42) versioned store and serving head, W-P1-PVER-07 initial import as version 1, W-P1-PVER-02 (#43) publish path for policy/settings/llmProviders writes, W-P1-PVER-08 version header, If-Match and 409 contract, W-P1-PVER-09 structural diff, W-P1-PVER-03 (#44) history and rollback APIs, W-P1-PVER-04 (#45) history panel, W-P1-PVER-05 (#233) mirror and drift, W-P1-PVER-10 fleet policy version and publish-log appends, W-P1-PVER-06 (#234) import/export CLI, W-P1-PVER-12 docs and release plan.

**Out of scope here:** importing the existing config as version 1 (W-P1-PVER-07), routing dashboard writes through the store (W-P1-PVER-02), HTTP concurrency headers (W-P1-PVER-08), history/rollback APIs (W-P1-PVER-03), mirroring head back into the YAML (W-P1-PVER-05), and the CLI (W-P1-PVER-06). Versioned mode needs the writable state-dir copy of the config (`--state-dir`); without `--state-dir` the CP stays in file mode and the dashboard keeps rewriting `--config` in place.

**What to build.** Migrations, `PolicyVersionStore` (an interface with a SQLite implementation so a later Postgres store can implement it), the flag, and a `policyServer` that serves the head doc with the live credential overlaid. Credential values are redacted before any row is written because the table is append-only.

**Requirements**

- Migrations (ID `policystore/0001`, registered through the cpstate runner of W-P1-SSO-01 and passed to the cpstate open call in `controlplane.Run` whenever a state dir is set, in either mode, so switching back to `--policy-store=file` never trips the cpstate downgrade guard; the tables stay empty in file mode): `policy_versions(version INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, parent_version, created_at, author_sub, author_email, author_kind, message, source, doc_json, doc_sha256)`, `policy_head(version)` seeded with one row at version 0, and `policy_publish_log(seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, version, etag, reason, actor_sub, at)`. The store exposes no update or delete of versions; a source-scan test enforces it.
- `PolicyVersionStore` interface: `Create(ctx, doc, author, msg, source, expectedHead) (version, changed, err)`, `Head`, `Get(version)` (exported so a later per-worker version selector needs no schema change), `List(cursor, limit)`, `PublishLog`. `author_kind` uses the admin-audit auth_method set (oidc|breakglass|cli|bearer|none|system). `message` is capped at 512 characters with control characters stripped.
- `Create` runs in one transaction (explicit BEGIN IMMEDIATE): insert the version, `UPDATE policy_head SET version=new WHERE version=expectedHead` as a cross-process compare-and-swap (0 rows returns `ErrConflict`, the transaction rolls back and nothing is written), append the publish_log row. A doc whose doc_sha256 equals head's writes nothing and returns changed=false. Ordering always uses the version integer, never created_at.
- Before hashing and storing, a non-empty `settings.secrets.secretAccessKey` is replaced by `sha256:<16 hex>` (exported `RedactCredentials(doc)` so approvals, W-P2-APPR-01, can reuse it). `blockedUsers` is never part of `doc_json` (the doc is the canonical `policyWire` {allowlist, denylist, settings}). The live credential stays in the CP-local served YAML `secretStore` block and is merged at serve time by a `credential` overlay registered through W-P1-PVER-11, so `/policy` bytes and worker behaviour are unchanged. The `/policy` ETag stays `etagFor(served wire)`, the hash of the merged wire, not doc_sha256.
- Validation reuses the existing loader instead of a parallel validator: `renderDocToRoot` (new, factored out of `Server.WritePolicy`/`WriteSettings` in internal/controlplane/controlplane.go) renders the candidate into a copy of the served YAML root and `validateDoc` writes a temp file and runs `config.NewLocalYAMLProvider`, the same check `atomicWriteConfig` makes. This enforces default-deny (an empty allowlist is rejected) and cross-block references. `Create` callers run validation first; failure returns a validation error and leaves head unchanged.
- Flag `--policy-store=file|versioned` (default `file`) in cmd/proxy/controlplane.go (parse only) -> `controlplane.Params.PolicyStore` -> `Config.PolicyStore`; wiring in `controlplane.Run`. `versioned` without `--state-dir` fails at startup with an actionable error; an unknown value is a startup error. In `file` mode, or in versioned mode with an empty store (head 0), `/policy` is byte-identical to today.
- Serving: `policyServer.loadPolicy` (internal/controlplane/policyserver.go) returns the head doc (decoded from doc_json, doc_sha256 checked) with the overlays applied, held in the in-memory `policyWatch`. The `/policy` hot path never reads the DB. `Create` calls `Refresh` so long-poll waiters wake at once. In versioned mode the existing 3 s ticker in `Server.Start` runs `SELECT version FROM policy_head` and reloads the doc only when the version changed, so writes from another process (the CLI) reach workers within 3 s plus one long-poll cycle.
- Fail closed at startup in versioned mode: the store cannot be read, head points at a missing version, or a doc fails its doc_sha256 check => the CP refuses to start with an actionable error and never falls back to the possibly older YAML. A runtime read error keeps the last-known-good wire in memory and logs. Workers are unaffected: they keep their last-known-good policy.
- slog `policy version created` logs version, parent, source, author_sub and doc_sha256 only; doc content, settings values and the credential are never logged.
- internal/controlplane/policystore.go is a new file in an existing package: no new package or Go module is added.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write the tests first: internal/controlplane/policystore_test.go (store, CAS race, redaction, DB-file scan, fail-closed startup) and extend controlplane_test.go for file-mode and empty-store byte identity.
2. New internal/controlplane/policystore.go: migrations, PolicyVersionStore interface, SQLite implementation (BEGIN IMMEDIATE, CAS update, publish_log append), ErrConflict, RedactCredentials and the `credential` overlay (reads the live value from the served YAML secretStore block).
3. internal/controlplane/controlplane.go: factor the block rendering of WritePolicy/WriteSettings into renderDocToRoot (new) and add validateDoc (new) reusing the temp-file and NewLocalYAMLProvider logic of atomicWriteConfig.
4. internal/controlplane/policyserver.go: when a store is set and Head() > 0, loadPolicy decodes doc_json, checks doc_sha256 and returns it (overlays from W-P1-PVER-11 apply); otherwise the YAML path. Cache the head version so Refresh reloads only when it changes.
5. cmd/proxy/controlplane.go: add the flag and Params.PolicyStore; internal/controlplane/run.go: open the migrations, build the store, fail-closed startup checks; Server.Start: poll the head version in versioned mode.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given head v3, Create with expectedHead=2 returns ErrConflict, the row count is unchanged and Head() is 3; with 20 goroutines racing Create on the same expectedHead under -race, exactly one succeeds: `go test -race ./internal/controlplane -run TestPolicyVersionStoreCAS`.
- [ ] Given a doc with an invalid domain pattern or an empty allowlist, validateDoc returns the loader error and Head() and the served ETag are unchanged: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestPolicyVersionValidate`.
- [ ] Given settings with secrets.secretAccessKey set, after Create the doc_json column and the DB file bytes do not contain the raw value while GET /policy still carries it, and blockedUsers served by a test overlay never appears in doc_json: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run 'TestPolicyVersionRedactsCredential|TestPolicyVersionExcludesOverlays'`.
- [ ] Given a long-poll waiter on the current ETag with wait=5s, Create with changed content wakes it with the new doc within 1s; Create with identical content writes no row and the ETag is unchanged: `go test -race ./internal/controlplane -run TestPolicyServerVersionedLongPoll`.
- [ ] Given `--policy-store=file` (default), or versioned with an empty store, GET /policy is byte-identical to a CP built from main on the same files: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestPolicyServerVersionedByteIdentity`.
- [ ] `--policy-store=versioned` without `--state-dir` and an unknown value exit non-zero before listening; an unreadable store, a head pointing at a missing version and a doc_sha256 mismatch refuse startup while a runtime read error keeps serving last-known-good: `go test ./internal/controlplane ./cmd/proxy -run 'TestPolicyStoreFlag|TestPolicyStoreFailClosedStartup|TestPolicyStoreRuntimeErrorKeepsLastGood'`.
- [ ] No log line from Create contains doc content or the credential (log capture), and no non-test file updates or deletes policy_versions rows: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run 'TestPolicyVersionLogsNoContent|TestPolicyStoreAppendOnly'`; `go test -race ./internal/controlplane` and `scripts/check.sh` pass.

### 2/12 · W-P1-PVER-02

**Route policy, settings and llmProviders writes through versioned publish**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#43](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/43)

**Context.** In versioned mode every writer of a wire-carried block (`WritePolicy`, `WriteSettings`, `WriteLLMProviders`) must create a policy version instead of rewriting the YAML in place; otherwise provider edits would save but never reach workers. This ticket adds the one publish path that builds the new doc from head and creates a version, and gives the dashboard writer setters a `context.Context` and write metadata so the author comes from the request's `Principal`. It was split from the original W-P1-PVER-02 (#43): the initial import is W-P1-PVER-07 and the HTTP concurrency contract (version header, If-Match, 409, audit hasher) is W-P1-PVER-08. Siblings in the Policy history + rollback feature (epic #41): W-P1-PVER-11 serve-time overlay seam, W-P1-PVER-01 (#42) versioned store and serving head, W-P1-PVER-07 initial import as version 1, W-P1-PVER-02 (#43) publish path for policy/settings/llmProviders writes, W-P1-PVER-08 version header, If-Match and 409 contract, W-P1-PVER-09 structural diff, W-P1-PVER-03 (#44) history and rollback APIs, W-P1-PVER-04 (#45) history panel, W-P1-PVER-05 (#233) mirror and drift, W-P1-PVER-10 fleet policy version and publish-log appends, W-P1-PVER-06 (#234) import/export CLI, W-P1-PVER-12 docs and release plan.

**Out of scope here:** reading `If-Match` or returning `version` in dashboard responses (W-P1-PVER-08), mirroring head into the YAML (W-P1-PVER-05), history APIs (W-P1-PVER-03). CP-local writers (`WriteIntegrations`, `WriteDetection`, console) keep the YAML round-trip.

**What to build.** `Server.publish`, the three rewritten writers, the `WriteMeta` plumbing through the dashboard setters and the `ConfigEditor` seam, and a field-ownership test.

**Requirements**

- `Server.publish(ctx, mutate func(*policyWire), meta WriteMeta, source string)` (new, internal/controlplane/controlplane.go) runs under `writeMu`: it reads head, applies `mutate`, validates with `validateDoc` (422-class error with the loader error on failure; head unchanged), and calls `PolicyVersionStore.Create` with `expectedHead` = `meta.ExpectedHead` or, when zero, the head read under writeMu; then `refresh()` and `reinjectExploreLLM()` as today. `ErrConflict` is returned to the caller.
- `WritePolicy` (allow/deny), `WriteSettings` (the blocks its form owns) and `WriteLLMProviders` (llmProviders; internal/controlplane/llmproviders_write.go) each change only their own fields and carry every other wire field from head (dlp, advisory, explore, judge, mcp, logging, cache and any field added later). `WriteSettings` keeps today's preserve-on-empty rule for secretAccessKey: an empty submitted value keeps the live credential (stored in the version only as its fingerprint); a non-empty value is written to the served YAML `secretStore.aws.secretAccessKey` (the existing round-trip of that one node) and only its fingerprint enters the doc. Version source values: `policy`, `settings`, `llmproviders`.
- A test asserts every `SettingsWire` field is either owned by a writer or listed as carried (a reflect-based table `TestSettingsFieldOwnership`), so a new field cannot be silently dropped by a publish.
- Dashboard setters take ctx and write metadata: `SetPolicyWriter(func(context.Context, config.Policy, WriteMeta) error)`, `SetSettingsWriter(func(context.Context, config.SettingsWire, WriteMeta) error)` (SSO-05 already gave it a ctx) and `SetLLMProvidersWriter(func(context.Context, []config.LLMProvider, WriteMeta) error)`; `WriteMeta{ExpectedHead int64; Message string}` (new, internal/dashboard). The handlers pass `WriteMeta{}` in this ticket; W-P1-PVER-08 fills it from `If-Match`. Update the `ConfigEditor` interface in internal/controlplane/seams.go and the wiring in controlplane.go.
- Author: a session `Principal` (SSO-04) records sub and email with author_kind `oidc`; a break-glass session records `breakglass:<username>` with kind `breakglass`; `console.auth: none` records `anonymous` with kind `none` (the CP admin bearer proves possession of the shared token, not an identity). The CLI (W-P1-PVER-06) records `cli:<os user>`; the import records `system:import`.
- CP-local readers that derive policy state use `s.policy.snapshot()` (the served wire), so after a versioned llmProviders edit `llmProvidersView()` and the explore LLM injection reflect head without reading the YAML blocks.
- In `file` mode all writers keep today's YAML round-trip unchanged, byte for byte.
- Every save logs the slog line from W-P1-PVER-01 and nothing else about content; the credential never appears in a log, error or response.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write the tests first in internal/controlplane (policy_publish_test.go) and update the dashboard setter tests for the new signatures.
2. internal/controlplane/controlplane.go: add Server.publish; rewrite WritePolicy and WriteSettings; internal/controlplane/llmproviders_write.go: rewrite WriteLLMProviders. Keep refresh() and reinjectExploreLLM().
3. internal/dashboard/dashboard.go: change SetPolicyWriter, SetSettingsWriter and SetLLMProvidersWriter to take ctx and WriteMeta (WriteMeta is new); handlers pass the request context and an empty WriteMeta.
4. internal/controlplane/seams.go: update ConfigEditor; controlplane.go wiring at dash.SetPolicyWriter / SetSettingsWriter / SetLLMProvidersWriter.
5. Add the field-ownership table test and update internal/dashboard/policy_edit_test.go, dashboard_llmproviders_test.go and internal/controlplane/llmproviders_write_test.go for the ctx setters. HTTP tests for dashboard writes authenticate like production: in `console.auth: none` with the CP dashboard-write bearer (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`; on main that is `Config.Token`, after W-P1-WTOK-07 `Config.AdminToken`, which falls back to `Config.Token`, so these tests need no change), and in oidc mode with a session fixture from the SSO tests. A write without credentials is refused by the guard and a test asserts it.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given a session Principal {sub:u1, email:a@x}, a policy save in versioned mode creates a version with author_sub=u1, author_email=a@x, author_kind=oidc and source `policy`; with console.auth none the author is `anonymous`: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestVersionedWriters`.
- [ ] Given a WriteLLMProviders edit in versioned mode, a new version with source `llmproviders` exists, GET /policy carries the new provider list and a long-poll waiter is woken: `go test -race ./internal/controlplane -run TestVersionedLLMProvidersReachWorkers`.
- [ ] Given a WriteSettings edit, the dlp and advisory blocks of the new version equal head's (carried, not dropped), and every SettingsWire field is owned or carried: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run 'TestVersionedSettingsCarryFields|TestSettingsFieldOwnership'`.
- [ ] Re-saving settings with an empty secretAccessKey keeps the live credential in GET /policy and stores only the fingerprint in the version; a new key lands in the served YAML secretStore and never in doc_json: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run 'TestVersionedSettingsPreserveCredential|TestVersionedSettingsNewCredential'`.
- [ ] An invalid edit (empty allowlist) returns the loader error, creates no version and leaves the ETag unchanged: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestVersionedPublishValidation`.
- [ ] Given `--policy-store=file`, the existing internal/controlplane and internal/dashboard tests pass with only signature updates: `go test -race ./internal/controlplane ./internal/dashboard`; `scripts/check.sh` passes.

### 3/12 · W-P1-PVER-03

**Add policy history, rollback and diff APIs**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#44](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/44)

**Context.** With versions being created (W-P1-PVER-02) admins need to see them and go back. This ticket adds dashboard APIs to list versions, fetch one version, diff two versions and roll back, behind the W-P1-SSO-05 role table. Because `internal/controlplane` imports `internal/dashboard`, the handlers talk to the store through a new `dashboard.PolicyHistory` interface. Rollback creates a new version and never touches credentials or the block list. It was split from the original W-P1-PVER-03 (#44): the structural diff itself is W-P1-PVER-09. Siblings in the Policy history + rollback feature (epic #41): W-P1-PVER-11 serve-time overlay seam, W-P1-PVER-01 (#42) versioned store and serving head, W-P1-PVER-07 initial import as version 1, W-P1-PVER-02 (#43) publish path for policy/settings/llmProviders writes, W-P1-PVER-08 version header, If-Match and 409 contract, W-P1-PVER-09 structural diff, W-P1-PVER-03 (#44) history and rollback APIs, W-P1-PVER-04 (#45) history panel, W-P1-PVER-05 (#233) mirror and drift, W-P1-PVER-10 fleet policy version and publish-log appends, W-P1-PVER-06 (#234) import/export CLI, W-P1-PVER-12 docs and release plan.

**Out of scope here:** the diff algorithm (W-P1-PVER-09), the UI (W-P1-PVER-04), approvals gating of rollback (W-P2-APPR-06).

**What to build.** Four routes, the `PolicyHistory` interface and setter, the controlplane adapter whose Rollback calls `Server.publish`, authz rows and audit.

**Requirements**

- `GET /dashboard/api/policy/versions?cursor=&limit=` returns metadata only (version, parent, created_at, author_sub, author_email, author_kind, message, source, doc_sha256), newest first, default 50, max 200. `GET /dashboard/api/policy/versions/{v}` returns the doc with credentials shown only as fingerprints. `GET .../versions/{v}/diff?against={u}` returns `DiffDocs` (W-P1-PVER-09) and defaults u to head.
- `POST .../versions/{v}/rollback` (editor, CSRF) requires `If-Match` (W-P1-PVER-08 contract), revalidates the target with `validateDoc` against today's rules, and creates latest+1 through `Server.publish` with source `rollback` and message `rollback to v<N>` plus an optional note from the body (<= 512 chars, control characters stripped). Content equal to head returns 200 with `changed=false` and creates no version. It keeps the current credential and the serve-time overlays (block list), since neither is part of the doc.
- Errors: unknown v 404, non-integer v 400, stale If-Match 409 (`policy_conflict`), missing If-Match 428, failed validation 422 with the loader error.
- New `dashboard.PolicyHistory` interface and `(*dashboard.Server).SetPolicyHistory` setter (internal/dashboard/dashboard.go); the four routes are registered only when it is set (workers and file mode return 404). New adapter internal/controlplane/policyhistory.go over `PolicyVersionStore`; wired in `Server.Handler` only when versioned. Register next to the existing routes (no routes.go exists yet; rule X9 baseline).
- Authz: every new route has an entry in the SSO-05 table (GET viewer; POST rollback editor); rollback is `Audited:true` with Action `policy.rollback`, Target `policy`, and denied attempts are recorded as outcome=denied by the W-P1-AAUD-02 middleware; the `policy` hasher from W-P1-PVER-08 records `v<from>:<sha>` and `v<to>:<sha>`.
- Rollback logs from_head, to_version, new_head and actor_sub, never doc contents. Responses never contain a raw credential.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write the tests first: internal/controlplane/policyhistory_test.go and internal/dashboard handler tests with a fake PolicyHistory. HTTP tests for dashboard writes authenticate like production: in `console.auth: none` with the CP dashboard-write bearer (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`; on main that is `Config.Token`, after W-P1-WTOK-07 `Config.AdminToken`, which falls back to `Config.Token`, so these tests need no change), and in oidc mode with a session fixture from the SSO tests. A write without credentials is refused by the guard and a test asserts it.
2. internal/dashboard/dashboard.go: add the PolicyHistory interface, SetPolicyHistory and the four routes.
3. New internal/controlplane/policyhistory.go: the adapter; Rollback builds the target doc and calls Server.publish with source `rollback`.
4. Add the four routes to dashboard.Routes() and the SSO-05 authz table (viewer for GET, editor for POST rollback, rollback Audited:true).

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given versions 1 to 3, an editor POST /versions/1/rollback with If-Match "v3" gives head=4, version 4's doc_sha256 equals version 1's, and a worker long-polling /policy receives the new ETag within one wait cycle: `go test -race ./internal/controlplane -run TestPolicyRollback`.
- [ ] Given a viewer session, list, get and diff return 200 and rollback returns 403 with an admin audit row outcome=denied: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestPolicyHistoryRoles`.
- [ ] Given a rollback, admin audit holds one row with target=policy, before=`v3:<sha>` and after=`v4:<sha>`; no response body or log line contains the raw secretAccessKey; a serve-time overlay (test overlay named blocked_users) is identical before and after: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run 'TestPolicyRollbackAudited|TestPolicyRollbackKeepsCredentialAndOverlays'`.
- [ ] Unknown v returns 404, a non-integer v 400, a stale If-Match 409, a missing If-Match 428, a target that no longer validates 422 with no new version: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestPolicyHistoryAPI`.
- [ ] In file mode and on a worker dashboard the four routes return 404: `go test ./internal/dashboard -run TestPolicyHistoryNotWired`; the route-coverage test passes: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestAuthzRouteCoverage`; `go test -race ./internal/controlplane ./internal/dashboard` and `scripts/check.sh` pass.

### 5/12 · W-P1-PVER-05

**Mirror head into the served YAML and detect external edits**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#233](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/233)

**Context.** In versioned mode the served YAML is no longer the source of policy, but turning the flag off or downgrading the binary must serve the same policy. This ticket keeps the YAML as a write-through mirror of head and detects hand edits to it (drift), which are warned about, shown in the dashboard and audited, but never served. It was split from the original W-P1-PVER-05 (#233): the fleet version lookup and publish-log appends are W-P1-PVER-10 and the documentation is W-P1-PVER-12. Siblings in the Policy history + rollback feature (epic #41): W-P1-PVER-11 serve-time overlay seam, W-P1-PVER-01 (#42) versioned store and serving head, W-P1-PVER-07 initial import as version 1, W-P1-PVER-02 (#43) publish path for policy/settings/llmProviders writes, W-P1-PVER-08 version header, If-Match and 409 contract, W-P1-PVER-09 structural diff, W-P1-PVER-03 (#44) history and rollback APIs, W-P1-PVER-04 (#45) history panel, W-P1-PVER-05 (#233) mirror and drift, W-P1-PVER-10 fleet policy version and publish-log appends, W-P1-PVER-06 (#234) import/export CLI, W-P1-PVER-12 docs and release plan.

**Out of scope here:** file-mode edit auditing (W-P1-AAUD-08, which this ticket reuses the helper of), the CLI import that brings an edited YAML back in (W-P1-PVER-06), and docs (W-P1-PVER-12).

**What to build.** `mirrorHead` after every head move, the drift check on the versioned ticker, the `drift` field and banner, and the audited external-edit record.

**Requirements**

- After each successful publish (and after a CLI-created version is picked up by the ticker), the CP writes head's policy and settings blocks (with the live credential, not the fingerprint) into the served YAML via `atomicWriteConfig` (`mirrorHead`, new, internal/controlplane/policystore.go, reusing `renderDocToRoot`) and records the mirrored file hash. The YAML therefore equals head, which makes `--policy-store=file` or a binary downgrade serve the same policy.
- A mirror failure (for example a read-only mount) logs at error with the version and never fails or rolls back the version.
- The versioned ticker compares the YAML policy/settings blocks (hash of the rendered blocks) with the mirrored hash. A difference is an external edit: log `served config policy block differs from head; ignored` once per distinct file hash with file_sha256 and head, keep serving head, and never serve the edit. External edits come back in only through `warden policy import` (W-P1-PVER-06).
- `GET /dashboard/api/policy` reports `drift: true` when an external edit is detected, and the UI shows a banner pointing to `warden policy import`. The banner clears when the YAML equals head again.
- When admin audit is enabled, each newly detected external edit appends one admin_audit row through the helper `auditExternalChange` of W-P1-AAUD-08 (auth_method system, action config.external_change, target policy, before `v<head>:<doc_sha256>`, after `file:<file_sha256>`), once per distinct file hash. In versioned mode the file-mode external-edit check of W-P1-AAUD-08 is not used (the file is not served); this drift check replaces it.
- Mirror writes go through `atomicWriteConfig`, so they are validated by the full loader and never leave a partial file; the mirrored hash is updated under `writeMu`.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write the tests first in internal/controlplane/policymirror_test.go (new).
2. internal/controlplane/policystore.go: add mirrorHead, called by Server.publish after a successful Create and by the head-poll path when the head version changes.
3. Extend the versioned ticker in Server.Start to hash the served YAML blocks and compare with the mirrored hash; call auditExternalChange (W-P1-AAUD-08) when audit is enabled.
4. Add the drift field to GET /dashboard/api/policy (internal/dashboard/dashboard.go) and the banner to internal/dashboard/index.html.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given versioned mode and three saves, the served YAML loaded with config.NewLocalYAMLProvider yields the same wire as head (credential included), and a CP restarted with `--policy-store=file` serves the same /policy bytes: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestPolicyMirror`.
- [ ] Given the served YAML made read-only, a save still creates a version and exactly one error line is logged: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestPolicyMirrorFailureNonFatal`.
- [ ] Given an external edit to the YAML policy block, /policy is unchanged after two ticker cycles, exactly one warning is logged, GET /dashboard/api/policy returns drift=true, and with admin audit enabled exactly one config.external_change row with `after file:<sha>` exists: `go test -race ./internal/controlplane -run 'TestPolicyDrift|TestPolicyDriftAudited'`.
- [ ] Restoring the YAML to head clears drift; the served HTML contains the drift banner text pointing to `warden policy import`: `go test ./internal/controlplane ./internal/dashboard -run 'TestPolicyDriftClears|TestPolicyDriftBannerServedHTML'`.
- [ ] `go test -race ./internal/controlplane ./internal/dashboard` and `scripts/check.sh` pass.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-PVER-02`](policy-versioning.md#212--w-p1-pver-02) Route policy, settings and llmProviders writes through versioned publish; [`W-P1-AAUD-08`](admin-audit-log.md#88--w-p1-aaud-08) Audit hand edits of the served YAML in file mode as config.external_change

**Unblocks:** [`W-P1-PVER-12`](policy-versioning.md#1212--w-p1-pver-12) Document the versioned policy store, mirror and release plan; [`W-P4-GOPS-04`](policy-as-code.md#511--w-p4-gops-04) Add staged versions and the rollout model

### 6/12 · W-P1-PVER-06

**Add warden policy import and export commands**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#234](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/234)

**Context.** Operators who manage policy as files need a way to create a version from a YAML file and to get a YAML out for downgrade, disaster recovery or GitOps hand-off, with the CP stopped or running. This ticket adds `warden policy import` and `warden policy export` under the existing `warden policy` command (cmd/proxy/policy.go `newPolicyCmd`). Import opens the cpstate DB directly and uses the same compare-and-swap `Create` as the CP, so a running CP picks the change up through head polling (3 s plus one long-poll cycle). CLI actions do not pass through HTTP, so they append admin audit rows directly through the shared opener `adminaudit.OpenForCLI` (W-P1-AAUD-05). Siblings in the Policy history + rollback feature (epic #41): W-P1-PVER-11 serve-time overlay seam, W-P1-PVER-01 (#42) versioned store and serving head, W-P1-PVER-07 initial import as version 1, W-P1-PVER-02 (#43) publish path for policy/settings/llmProviders writes, W-P1-PVER-08 version header, If-Match and 409 contract, W-P1-PVER-09 structural diff, W-P1-PVER-03 (#44) history and rollback APIs, W-P1-PVER-04 (#45) history panel, W-P1-PVER-05 (#233) mirror and drift, W-P1-PVER-10 fleet policy version and publish-log appends, W-P1-PVER-06 (#234) import/export CLI, W-P1-PVER-12 docs and release plan.

**Out of scope here:** the P4 `warden policy lint` and repo sync (W-P4-GOPS-01/02) and approvals gating of imports (W-P2-APPR-06).

**What to build.** Two cobra subcommands that stay thin (rule C1), plus exported wrappers in `internal/controlplane` for the store constructor and `validateDoc`.

**Requirements**

- `warden policy import --state-dir <dir> --file <yaml> [--message m] [--admin-audit-key-file F]` decodes the file strictly (yaml.v3 KnownFields), validates with the same `validateDoc`, redacts the credential, and calls `Create` with `expectedHead` = current head and author `cli:<os user>`, source `import`. It requires the versioned store to exist in the state DB (a clear error otherwise).
- Import of content equal to head prints `no change` and exits 0; a conflict prints the new head and exits non-zero; a validation failure exits non-zero naming the file and the loader message only.
- Import appends an admin audit row with actor `cli:<os user>`, auth_method cli, action `policy.import`, target `policy`, before `v<head>:<sha>` and after `v<new>:<sha>` through `adminaudit.OpenForCLI` (W-P1-AAUD-05): a nil Recorder (table absent) skips the append with a one-line notice; a missing or mismatching key aborts before the version is created.
- `warden policy export --state-dir <dir> [--version N]` opens the DB read-only and writes to stdout a loadable config YAML with the top-level keys policy, settings and llmProviders of that version, with the credential fingerprint left out.
- Neither command prints credential values; errors name the file and loader message only. A `secretAccessKey` that is not a fingerprint in an imported file is stored as its fingerprint, and the live value is never printed.
- internal/controlplane gains exported wrappers (`OpenPolicyStore(ctx, stateDir)`, `ValidatePolicyDocFile`) so cmd/proxy holds no business logic.

**Implementation plan**

### 7/12 · W-P1-PVER-07

**Import the served config as version 1 on first versioned start**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue —

**Context.** An existing deployment that switches to `--policy-store=versioned` already has a served config.yaml with allow/deny policy and settings. The store must start with that policy as version 1, so workers keep the exact policy and ETag they have and no worker reports `behind`. This ticket was split from the original W-P1-PVER-02 (#43, the '43a' in the 2026-10-19 audit). It runs once, only in versioned mode with an empty store. Siblings in the Policy history + rollback feature (epic #41): W-P1-PVER-11 serve-time overlay seam, W-P1-PVER-01 (#42) versioned store and serving head, W-P1-PVER-07 initial import as version 1, W-P1-PVER-02 (#43) publish path for policy/settings/llmProviders writes, W-P1-PVER-08 version header, If-Match and 409 contract, W-P1-PVER-09 structural diff, W-P1-PVER-03 (#44) history and rollback APIs, W-P1-PVER-04 (#45) history panel, W-P1-PVER-05 (#233) mirror and drift, W-P1-PVER-10 fleet policy version and publish-log appends, W-P1-PVER-06 (#234) import/export CLI, W-P1-PVER-12 docs and release plan.

**Out of scope here:** routing later edits through the store (W-P1-PVER-02), the CLI import (W-P1-PVER-06), and any change to the served YAML (it already equals the imported doc).

**What to build.** `importInitialVersion`, called at CP startup in versioned mode when `Head()==0`.

**Requirements**

- `importInitialVersion` (new, internal/controlplane/policystore.go), called from `controlplane.Run`/`New` when the store is versioned and `Head()==0`: build the doc from the served YAML (`allowlist`, `denylist`, `config.SettingsWireFromPolicy` with the credential redacted by `RedactCredentials`; never `blockedUsers`), validate it with `validateDoc`, and `Create` version 1 with author_sub `system:import`, author_kind `system`, source `import`, message `initial import from <path>`.
- The served wire must not change: compare `etagFor(served wire)` before and after the import; a mismatch fails startup with an actionable error (fail closed) and writes nothing that is left half-applied (Create is one transaction). `/policy` bytes and ETag are identical before and after, so no worker reports `behind`.
- Idempotent: a non-empty store is never re-imported, and a restart after a successful import does nothing. A second CP process starting against the same state DB (a race at first start) imports at most once because Create is a compare-and-swap from head 0.
- When `cfg.AdminAudit` is set, append one admin audit row directly through the Recorder (the HTTP middleware does not see startup): action `policy.initial_import`, target `policy`, auth_method `system`, actor `system`, before_hash `file:<sha256 of the served YAML>`, after_hash `v1:<doc_sha256>`. A Recorder error is logged at ERROR and does not stop startup.
- slog `policy version created` (from W-P1-PVER-01) is the only log line; it carries version, source and doc_sha256, never content.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write the tests first in internal/controlplane/policystore_import_test.go (state dir with a populated config.yaml).
2. internal/controlplane/policystore.go: add importInitialVersion; internal/controlplane/run.go (or New): call it in versioned mode when Head()==0, compare etagFor before and after.
3. Append the audit row through cfg.AdminAudit when non-nil.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given a state dir with a populated config.yaml and an empty store, starting with `--policy-store=versioned` serves /policy byte-identical to file mode with the same ETag, and the store holds exactly one version authored `system:import`: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestPolicyMigrationByteIdentical`.
- [ ] A second start on the same state dir does not create another version, and two CPs racing the first start create one: `go test -race ./internal/controlplane -run 'TestPolicyImportIdempotent|TestPolicyImportRace'`.
- [ ] A served config whose import would change the served ETag (test fake) fails startup with the actionable error and leaves the store empty: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestPolicyImportEtagMismatchFailsStartup`.
- [ ] With admin audit enabled the import writes one `policy.initial_import` row with after_hash `v1:<doc_sha256>`; the doc stored contains no secretAccessKey value: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run 'TestPolicyImportAudited|TestPolicyImportRedacts'`; `scripts/check.sh` passes.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-PVER-01`](policy-versioning.md#112--w-p1-pver-01) Add versioned policy store and serve the head version; [`W-P1-AAUD-05`](admin-audit-log.md#58--w-p1-aaud-05) Gate admin audit behind config, check the key id at startup, add segment rotation and a shared CLI recorder opener

### 8/12 · W-P1-PVER-08

**Add the version header, If-Match and 409 contract and the policy audit hasher**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue —

**Context.** Two editors can open the policy tab at once; in versioned mode a save must name the head it was based on, and a stale save must fail with a body that names the conflicting author. This ticket adds that HTTP contract on top of the publish path (W-P1-PVER-02) and registers the `policy` state hasher so HTTP saves record before/after hashes in the admin audit log. It was split from the original W-P1-PVER-02 (#43, the '43c' in the 2026-10-19 audit). Siblings in the Policy history + rollback feature (epic #41): W-P1-PVER-11 serve-time overlay seam, W-P1-PVER-01 (#42) versioned store and serving head, W-P1-PVER-07 initial import as version 1, W-P1-PVER-02 (#43) publish path for policy/settings/llmProviders writes, W-P1-PVER-08 version header, If-Match and 409 contract, W-P1-PVER-09 structural diff, W-P1-PVER-03 (#44) history and rollback APIs, W-P1-PVER-04 (#45) history panel, W-P1-PVER-05 (#233) mirror and drift, W-P1-PVER-10 fleet policy version and publish-log appends, W-P1-PVER-06 (#234) import/export CLI, W-P1-PVER-12 docs and release plan.

**Out of scope here:** the UI that sends the headers and the 428 for a missing If-Match (W-P1-PVER-04), rollback (W-P1-PVER-03), and the audit middleware itself (W-P1-AAUD-02).

**What to build.** Version in GET bodies and an `X-Warden-Policy-Version` header, `If-Match` parsing into `WriteMeta.ExpectedHead`, the 409 `policy_conflict` mapping, and the `policy` StateHasher.

**Requirements**

- `GET /dashboard/api/policy` and `GET /dashboard/api/settings` (and the llmproviders GET) return `version` in the body and an `X-Warden-Policy-Version: N` header in versioned mode; in file mode neither is present (bodies unchanged).
- Writes (`PUT /dashboard/api/policy`, settings, llmproviders) read `If-Match: "v<N>"` into `WriteMeta.ExpectedHead`. A stale value returns 409 `{error:"policy_conflict", head, author}` where author is the head version's author (409, not 412, so the body can name the conflicting author). Policy, settings and llmProviders share one head, so a settings save makes a concurrent allow/deny save conflict. A malformed If-Match returns 400. A missing If-Match is accepted for now so today's UI keeps working; W-P1-PVER-04 makes it 428 in versioned mode. `/policy`'s content-hash ETag is unchanged.
- When `cfg.AdminAudit` is set, register a `policy` StateHasher (W-P1-AAUD-02 `RegisterStateHasher`) returning `v<head>:<doc_sha256>`, replacing the built-in YAML policy hasher in versioned mode, so HTTP saves record before and after as `v<N>:<sha>`. The conflict (409) is recorded as outcome `rejected` by the middleware.
- The 409 body contains author sub/email only for authenticated console users (writes are authenticated) and never doc content.
- internal/dashboard stays free of controlplane imports: the head version and author reach the handlers through the `WriteMeta`/`ErrConflict` types or a small interface set with the writers.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write the tests first: internal/dashboard/policy_conflict_test.go (handlers with fake writers) and internal/controlplane/policy_contract_test.go. HTTP tests for dashboard writes authenticate like production: in `console.auth: none` with the CP dashboard-write bearer (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`; on main that is `Config.Token`, after W-P1-WTOK-07 `Config.AdminToken`, which falls back to `Config.Token`, so these tests need no change), and in oidc mode with a session fixture from the SSO tests. A write without credentials is refused by the guard and a test asserts it.
2. internal/dashboard/dashboard.go: add version field and header to the three GET handlers when the writer reports a version; parse If-Match in putPolicy, putSettings and the llmproviders handler; map the controlplane conflict error to 409.
3. internal/controlplane: translate PolicyVersionStore.ErrConflict into the dashboard-visible conflict error with head and author; register the `policy` StateHasher in Server.Handler when versioned and cfg.AdminAudit != nil.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given two saves from head v5, the second gets 409 with `author` and `head`; replaying a POST with the old If-Match returns 409 and creates no version: `go test ./internal/dashboard ./internal/controlplane -run 'TestPolicyWriteConflict|TestPolicyIfMatchStale'`.
- [ ] Given a session Principal {sub:u1, email:a@x}, a save with the current If-Match creates a version with author_sub=u1; a malformed If-Match returns 400; a settings save makes a concurrent policy save conflict: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run 'TestPolicyIfMatchCurrent|TestPolicyIfMatchMalformed|TestSharedHeadConflict'`.
- [ ] In file mode GET /dashboard/api/policy has no `version` field and no header, and saves without If-Match still succeed: `go test ./internal/dashboard -run TestPolicyFileModeNoVersion`.
- [ ] With admin audit enabled a versioned save writes one row with before `v<N>:<sha>` and after `v<N+1>:<sha>`; a 409 writes an outcome=rejected row: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run 'TestPolicyHasherVersioned|TestPolicyConflictAudited'`; `go test -race ./internal/dashboard ./internal/controlplane` and `scripts/check.sh` pass.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-PVER-02`](policy-versioning.md#212--w-p1-pver-02) Route policy, settings and llmProviders writes through versioned publish; [`W-P1-AAUD-02`](admin-audit-log.md#28--w-p1-aaud-02) Record CP admin mutations through audit middleware

**Unblocks:** [`W-P1-PVER-03`](policy-versioning.md#312--w-p1-pver-03) Add policy history, rollback and diff APIs; [`W-P1-PVER-04`](policy-versioning.md#412--w-p1-pver-04) Add history panel with diff view and rollback to dashboard; [`W-P1-PVER-12`](policy-versioning.md#1212--w-p1-pver-12) Document the versioned policy store, mirror and release plan

### 9/12 · W-P1-PVER-09

**Add structural policy diff and DiffKey on allow/deny entries**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue —

**Context.** History and approvals both need to say what a policy change did, not show a text diff. This ticket adds a pure structural diff over two policy docs and the `DiffKey()` method that identifies allow/deny entries, so later features (the history API W-P1-PVER-03, the history panel, P2 approvals' widening classification W-P2-APPR-02, W-P1-GPOL-01 adding groups/users to the key) share one definition. It was split from the original W-P1-PVER-03 (#44) because it is a pure function with no store or HTTP dependency. Siblings in the Policy history + rollback feature (epic #41): W-P1-PVER-11 serve-time overlay seam, W-P1-PVER-01 (#42) versioned store and serving head, W-P1-PVER-07 initial import as version 1, W-P1-PVER-02 (#43) publish path for policy/settings/llmProviders writes, W-P1-PVER-08 version header, If-Match and 409 contract, W-P1-PVER-09 structural diff, W-P1-PVER-03 (#44) history and rollback APIs, W-P1-PVER-04 (#45) history panel, W-P1-PVER-05 (#233) mirror and drift, W-P1-PVER-10 fleet policy version and publish-log appends, W-P1-PVER-06 (#234) import/export CLI, W-P1-PVER-12 docs and release plan.

**Out of scope here:** serving the diff over HTTP (W-P1-PVER-03) and rendering it (W-P1-PVER-04).

**What to build.** `DiffKey()` on the config entries and `DiffDocs(a, b policyWire) PolicyDiff` in a new file.

**Requirements**

- internal/config/config.go (existing): add the exported method `DiffKey() string` on `AllowlistEntry` and `DenylistEntry`, returning `domain|port` today (rateLimit and timeWindow are compared attributes, not part of the key). It is exported from the start because the diff lives in internal/controlplane (the original plan named it `diffKey()`, which cannot be called across packages; W-P2-APPR-02's rename step is therefore already done). W-P1-GPOL-01 extends the key with groups/users.
- internal/controlplane/policydiff.go (new): `DiffDocs(a, b policyWire) PolicyDiff{Allow, Deny []EntryChange; Settings []PathChange}`. Allow and deny lists are multisets keyed by DiffKey (duplicates show as count changes with occurrence counting); a rateLimit/timeWindow difference on the same key is `changed`; entries only in b are `added`, only in a `removed`. Order of the output is deterministic (sorted by key).
- Settings are compared by JSON path with a generic JSON-map walk into {added, removed, changed} (arrays compared as whole values at their path). Credential paths (`settings.secrets.secretAccessKey`) show only the fingerprints, never a raw value: the diff operates on redacted docs and refuses (returns an error) if a non-fingerprint value is found at a credential path.
- No I/O, no clock, no logging of doc content; the function is allocation-bounded by doc size and safe for concurrent use.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write policydiff_test.go first.
2. internal/config/config.go: add DiffKey() on AllowlistEntry and DenylistEntry.
3. New internal/controlplane/policydiff.go: DiffDocs, EntryChange, PathChange, PolicyDiff.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] policydiff_test.go covers allow added, removed and changed (rateLimit), duplicate entries as count changes, a deny change, a nested settings change (judge.model), and a secretAccessKey change shown only as a fingerprint change: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestPolicyDiff`.
- [ ] A raw (non-fingerprint) secretAccessKey in either doc makes DiffDocs return an error and the error text does not contain the value: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestPolicyDiffRefusesRawCredential`.
- [ ] Output order is stable across 100 runs on a shuffled input: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestPolicyDiffDeterministic`; `go test -race ./internal/config ./internal/controlplane` and `scripts/check.sh` pass.

### 10/12 · W-P1-PVER-10

**Map worker ETags to policy versions and log ETag-only changes**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue —

**Context.** The fleet view should say which policy version each worker runs, but workers report an ETag, and the served ETag can change without a new version (a block-list edit, an AWS credential rotation, later the agent registry). This ticket records every served-ETag change in `policy_publish_log` and maps heartbeat ETags back to versions, so an up-to-date worker never shows as `unknown`. It was split from the original W-P1-PVER-05 (#233, the '233b' in the 2026-10-19 audit). P2 signed bundles take `policy_publish_log.seq` as their monotonic number and read this path. Siblings in the Policy history + rollback feature (epic #41): W-P1-PVER-11 serve-time overlay seam, W-P1-PVER-01 (#42) versioned store and serving head, W-P1-PVER-07 initial import as version 1, W-P1-PVER-02 (#43) publish path for policy/settings/llmProviders writes, W-P1-PVER-08 version header, If-Match and 409 contract, W-P1-PVER-09 structural diff, W-P1-PVER-03 (#44) history and rollback APIs, W-P1-PVER-04 (#45) history panel, W-P1-PVER-05 (#233) mirror and drift, W-P1-PVER-10 fleet policy version and publish-log appends, W-P1-PVER-06 (#234) import/export CLI, W-P1-PVER-12 docs and release plan.

**Out of scope here:** the mirror/drift (W-P1-PVER-05), any concrete overlay (W-P1-BLOCK-03 adds the block list; this ticket's tests use a test overlay), and metrics.

**What to build.** `PolicyVersionStore.AppendPublish`, the Refresh hook that calls it, the ETag-to-version lookup and the `policyVersion` field in the fleet view.

**Requirements**

- `PolicyVersionStore.AppendPublish(ctx, etag, reason, actor string)` and `VersionForETag(ctx, etag) (version int64, ok bool)` (internal/controlplane/policystore.go). The lookup returns the version of the most recent publish_log row with that etag.
- `policyServer.Refresh` calls `AppendPublish` (versioned mode only) when the served ETag changed and the head version did not (a `Create` appends its own publish_log row, so Refresh finds the latest row's etag already equal and appends nothing). The reason is the name of the first overlay (W-P1-PVER-11 `overlayFingerprints`) whose fingerprint changed (`credential`, `blocked_users`, ...), else `external`; actor `system`. A repeated Refresh with the same ETag appends nothing.
- The fleet API (`WorkerView`, internal/dashboard/dashboard.go) gains `policyVersion` (int, omitted when unknown) filled by mapping the heartbeat `policyETag` (`handleHeartbeat` already records it) through `VersionForETag`; an unknown ETag shows as unknown and `behind` is unchanged. File mode adds no field.
- The lookup runs only when the dashboard builds the worker list, never on the heartbeat or `/policy` hot paths; results for one list call are cached in memory.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write the tests first in internal/controlplane/policy_fleetversion_test.go using a test overlay named blocked_users.
2. internal/controlplane/policystore.go: AppendPublish and VersionForETag. internal/controlplane/policyserver.go Refresh: detect ETag-only changes using overlayFingerprints.
3. internal/controlplane/controlplane.go (worker view closure): fill policyVersion; internal/dashboard/dashboard.go: add the WorkerView field.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given a worker heartbeat with the ETag of v2 while head is v4, the fleet API shows policyVersion 2 and behind=true: `go test -race ./internal/controlplane -run TestFleetPolicyVersion`.
- [ ] Given an overlay change after v4 (test overlay), exactly one publish_log row with reason `blocked_users` and version 4 is appended, a worker heartbeating the new ETag shows version 4 (not unknown), and a second Refresh appends nothing: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestFleetPolicyVersionOverlay`.
- [ ] Unblocking back to the previous ETag appends a new row (seq moves forward) and maps to version 4; an unknown ETag shows no policyVersion: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run 'TestPublishLogEtagReturns|TestFleetPolicyVersionUnknown'`.
- [ ] In file mode no publish_log row and no policyVersion field exist (existing tests pass); `go test -race ./internal/controlplane ./internal/dashboard` and `scripts/check.sh` pass.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-PVER-01`](policy-versioning.md#112--w-p1-pver-01) Add versioned policy store and serve the head version; [`W-P1-PVER-11`](policy-versioning.md#1112--w-p1-pver-11) Add serve-time wire overlays to the policy server

### 11/12 · W-P1-PVER-11

**Add serve-time wire overlays to the policy server**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue —

**Context.** The policy server builds the wire (`policyWire`) from the served YAML (today) or from a policy version (W-P1-PVER-01). Some data must be merged into the served wire at serve time but must never be stored in a policy version, because a rollback would otherwise restore it: the AWS credential (W-P1-PVER-01), the block list (W-P1-BLOCK-03) and, in P2, the agent registry. This ticket adds that one seam, so those features do not each edit `loadPolicy` and do not depend on each other. It adds no overlay itself and changes no behaviour. Siblings in the Policy history + rollback feature (epic #41): W-P1-PVER-11 serve-time overlay seam, W-P1-PVER-01 (#42) versioned store and serving head, W-P1-PVER-07 initial import as version 1, W-P1-PVER-02 (#43) publish path for policy/settings/llmProviders writes, W-P1-PVER-08 version header, If-Match and 409 contract, W-P1-PVER-09 structural diff, W-P1-PVER-03 (#44) history and rollback APIs, W-P1-PVER-04 (#45) history panel, W-P1-PVER-05 (#233) mirror and drift, W-P1-PVER-10 fleet policy version and publish-log appends, W-P1-PVER-06 (#234) import/export CLI, W-P1-PVER-12 docs and release plan.

**Out of scope here:** any concrete overlay (W-P1-PVER-01 registers `credential`, W-P1-BLOCK-03 registers `blocked_users`) and publish-log appends on overlay changes (W-P1-PVER-10).

**What to build.** An ordered list of named overlays applied by `policyServer.loadPolicy` after the base wire is built, with each overlay's fingerprint kept next to the served snapshot.

**Requirements**

- internal/controlplane/policyserver.go (existing): `type wireOverlay struct { name string; apply func(ctx context.Context, w *policyWire) (fingerprint string, err error) }` and `(*policyServer).addOverlay(o wireOverlay) error`, callable only during wiring (before the first `Refresh`/`ServePolicy`); a duplicate or empty name returns an error.
- `loadPolicy` builds the base wire exactly as today, then applies the overlays in registration order. Any overlay error fails `loadPolicy`, so `Refresh` keeps the last-known-good wire and ETag (existing behaviour for load errors) and logs the overlay name and a bounded error, never wire content.
- The fingerprints (`map[string]string`, overlay name to opaque string; empty string = the overlay contributes nothing) of the last successful load are stored in the same `policyWatch` snapshot as the wire and ETag and are readable through `ps.overlayFingerprints()` for W-P1-PVER-10.
- Overlays run only on `Refresh` (writes and the 3 s ticker), never per `/policy` request: the hot path stays free of overlay work and I/O.
- With no overlays registered, `/policy` bytes and ETag are identical to main (golden test).

**Implementation plan**

1. Write the tests first in internal/controlplane/policyserver_overlay_test.go.
2. internal/controlplane/policyserver.go: add wireOverlay, addOverlay, the overlay loop in loadPolicy and the fingerprint map in policyWatch.set/snapshot.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] With no overlay, GET /policy body and ETag equal a golden captured on main: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestPolicyOverlayNoneIsByteIdentical`.
- [ ] Two overlays run in registration order and a later overlay sees the earlier one's change; their fingerprints are returned by overlayFingerprints: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run 'TestPolicyOverlayOrder|TestPolicyOverlayFingerprints'`.
- [ ] An overlay that returns an error leaves the served ETag and body unchanged (last-known-good) and long-poll waiters are not woken: `go test -race ./internal/controlplane -run TestPolicyOverlayErrorKeepsLastGood`.
- [ ] A duplicate or empty overlay name is rejected: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestPolicyOverlayRejectsDuplicate`; `go test -race ./internal/controlplane` and `scripts/check.sh` pass.

### 12/12 · W-P1-PVER-12

**Document the versioned policy store, mirror and release plan**

Type **docs** · Size **S** · Issue —

**Context.** Policy history changes how operators think about the served YAML, so the behaviour and the rollout need one place in the docs. This ticket documents the feature once its pieces exist. It was split from the original W-P1-PVER-05 (#233), where the documentation requirement was mixed in with code. Siblings in the Policy history + rollback feature (epic #41): W-P1-PVER-11 serve-time overlay seam, W-P1-PVER-01 (#42) versioned store and serving head, W-P1-PVER-07 initial import as version 1, W-P1-PVER-02 (#43) publish path for policy/settings/llmProviders writes, W-P1-PVER-08 version header, If-Match and 409 contract, W-P1-PVER-09 structural diff, W-P1-PVER-03 (#44) history and rollback APIs, W-P1-PVER-04 (#45) history panel, W-P1-PVER-05 (#233) mirror and drift, W-P1-PVER-10 fleet policy version and publish-log appends, W-P1-PVER-06 (#234) import/export CLI, W-P1-PVER-12 docs and release plan.

**Out of scope here:** any code; every claim in the docs must match merged behaviour.

**What to build.** A 'Policy history' section in docs/control-plane.md.

**Requirements**

- docs/control-plane.md documents: the `--policy-store=file|versioned` flag and the `--state-dir` requirement (file mode without a state dir keeps editing `--config` in place); the migration to version 1; the append-only store and what it never holds (credential values, block list); the If-Match / 409 / 428 contract and the version header; history, diff and rollback; the write-through mirror, drift detection and `warden policy import`/`export`; the fleet policy version column; and the downgrade path (`--policy-store=file` serves the mirrored YAML).
- The release plan: release N ships versioned only behind `--policy-store=versioned` (default `file`); release N+1 flips the default to `versioned` (`--policy-store=file` stays as an explicit opt-out, and a CP started without `--state-dir` keeps file mode with a startup WARN); release N+2 removes YAML as a policy source (`--policy-store=file` is removed, the served YAML is only the write-through mirror of head, and hand edits are never served).
- State plainly which behaviour is audited (`policy.*` rows, `config.external_change`) and that credentials appear in history only as fingerprints.

**Implementation plan**

1. Add the section to docs/control-plane.md, then run `go run docs/roadmap/gen.go check` (no roadmap data changes here) and a link check by eye on cross-references.
2. Add a Go test that greps docs/control-plane.md for each flag and route name the section must mention, so it cannot drift from the code: internal/controlplane/docs_policy_test.go.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] docs/control-plane.md contains the flag names, the three release-plan statements and each route (`/dashboard/api/policy/versions`, `.../rollback`, `.../diff`): `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestPolicyHistoryDocsMentionSurface`.
- [ ] Every flag and route the docs name exists in code (the test resolves `--policy-store`, `warden policy import|export` and the route strings against the source): same test.
- [ ] The docs name the audit actions `policy.initial_import`, `policy.rollback` and `config.external_change` and state that credentials appear in history only as fingerprints: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestPolicyHistoryDocsAudit`; `scripts/check.sh` passes.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-PVER-03`](policy-versioning.md#312--w-p1-pver-03) Add policy history, rollback and diff APIs; [`W-P1-PVER-05`](policy-versioning.md#512--w-p1-pver-05) Mirror head into the served YAML and detect external edits; [`W-P1-PVER-06`](policy-versioning.md#612--w-p1-pver-06) Add warden policy import and export commands; [`W-P1-PVER-08`](policy-versioning.md#812--w-p1-pver-08) Add the version header, If-Match and 409 contract and the policy audit hasher; [`W-P1-PVER-10`](policy-versioning.md#1012--w-p1-pver-10) Map worker ETags to policy versions and log ETag-only changes
